processing_steps.method: air induction melting with flux cover (AIMFC)
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Flux cover of Al2O3, CaO, MgO and CaF2 with proprietary charging schedule; top poured into split cast iron molds. Forty-kilogram melts of five carbon-series alloys (including Fe-7Al-0.5C) were prepared by AIMFC.
Hot forged in a 1-tonne pneumatic forge hammer with die platens at room temperature; carbon-series ingots were hot forged (b0061).
Final hot-rolled plate thickness 12 mm; 1-mm reduction per pass; samples reheated after every six rolling passes. Carbon-series ingots hot rolled to 12 mm thickness (b0061).

structures.overall_structure: Hot-rolled Fe-7Al-0.5C plate with a Fe3Al matrix containing a dense, banded distribution of Fe3AlC0.5 precipitates aligned along the rolling direction; precipitate volume fraction is significant and increases with carbon content.

phases_present.morphology: dense, banded, dark precipitates aligned along the rolling direction

precipitates.distribution: dense, banded, aligned along rolling direction

interfaces.phase_evolution: Fe3AlC0.5 precipitates form on carbon addition; their volume fraction increases significantly with increasing carbon content.

comparative_performance.comparison_metric: Addition of 0.5 wt.% C to Fe-7Al (hot-rolled) raises UTS to 928 ± 6.8 MPa and YS to 652 ± 7.5 MPa (vs 425 ± 4.5 MPa UTS and 382 ± 6.3 MPa YS at 0.002 wt.% C) while reducing total elongation to 08 ± 1.1 % (vs 21 ± 2.2 % at 0.002 wt.% C).

characterization_methods.purpose: Measure alloy composition of Fe-7Al-0.5C prepared by AIMFC.
Confirm precipitate phase in higher-carbon Fe-7Al alloys.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Fe3Al and Fe3AlC0.5 peaks observed for the 0.15 wt.% C alloy; similar peaks observed in the three other alloys with 0.35-1 wt.% C (including Fe-7Al-0.5C), confirming Fe3AlC0.5 precipitates.

characterization_methods.purpose: Observe microstructure of hot-rolled Fe-7Al-0.5C plate.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Dense, banded dark precipitate aligned along the rolling direction (Fig. 5d).

characterization_methods.technique: room-temperature tensile testing and bulk hardness measurement
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Room temperature; values reported as mean ± standard deviation.
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure room-temperature tensile properties and hardness of hot-rolled Fe-7Al-0.5C.
characterization_methods.key_findings: Bulk hardness 275 ± 9.2 HV; UTS 928 ± 6.8 MPa; YS 652 ± 7.5 MPa; total elongation 08 ± 1.1 %.

unmapped_findings: Measured chemical composition of Fe-7Al-0.5C (Table IV): Al 6.95, Si 0.15, Mn 0.12, S 0.004, C 0.50 wt.%.
Table V caption labels the carbon-series route 'AIM', but the section text (b0060) states these alloys were prepared by air induction melting with a flux cover (AIMFC).
Precipitation hardening by hard Fe3AlC0.5 is reported as the predominant strengthening mechanism in the carbon-series alloys (b0062).

The paper (b0062) states carbon addition to Fe-7 wt.% Al improved room-temperature strength (396-610 MPa) and decreased elongation (18-3%); these summary ranges are not consistent with the tabulated Table V values for the individual carbon-series alloys and were not used as sample property values.
The largest strength jump in the carbon series occurs between Fe-7Al-0.35C and Fe-7Al-0.5C (UTS 515→928 MPa, YS 480→652 MPa), while total elongation drops from 13% to 8% (Table V).
